punchline: Tom Waits told a song that arrived while he was driving to go and bother Leonard Cohen instead.
thirty_sec: In Big Magic, Elizabeth Gilbert tells how Tom Waits, driving on an LA freeway, felt a song arrive with no way to write it down. Instead of panicking, he spoke to it: can't you see I'm driving? Come back later, or go bother Leonard Cohen. His anxiety eased. Gilbert's point: creativity can be a lighter, even humorous collaboration rather than a torment you carry alone.
question: What happens inside you when an idea arrives at the wrong moment?
